title: Target anatomy
view: The back of the skull, head at the top, zoomed on the right half; seen from behind, so the patient's right is on the image right.
teachingPoint: One-third of the way from the external occipital protuberance to the mastoid, on the superior nuchal line, the greater occipital nerve reaches the scalp just medial to the occipital artery: enter there, perpendicular, to bone.
claims: Back of the skull, patient's right on the image right (seen from behind).
Dashed line from the external occipital protuberance to the mastoid, with the one-third mark (record steps; Arata 2024; ASRA 2019).

Greater occipital nerve (yellow) reaching the scalp at the superior nuchal line about 2 cm lateral to the protuberance; dashed below the line where it is deep, rising from C2 between obliquus capitis inferior and semispinalis (record anatomy).
Occipital artery (red) just lateral to the nerve at the line (record anatomy); its course on the scalp is schematic.
Red dot: the entry point just medial to the artery at the one-third mark (record steps).
Labels: Greater occipital nerve, Occipital artery, External occipital protuberance, Mastoid, Superior nuchal line, One-third.

geometry.why: midline on the image left, the right mastoid on the image right (seen from behind)
the nerve lies just medial to the artery
the one-third mark sits on the protuberance-mastoid line
